context: A talk at the reopening of Wrenbury Central Library

cues.t: Part 2. You will hear the head librarian giving a talk to local residents at the reopening of a town library. First you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.

Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming to this first look at Wrenbury Central Library. I'm Karen Doyle, the head librarian, and after eighteen months behind scaffolding, I'm delighted to be able to show you what we've done.

Let me begin with why the building closed at all. Many people assumed we simply wanted room for more computers, and others told me they'd heard that visitor numbers had collapsed. Neither is true. In fact, our visitor numbers held up very well. The work became necessary when surveyors inspected the building and found that the old roof was no longer safe. Once that repair had begun, it made sense to modernise the rest of the library at the same time.

Now, what does all this mean for members? Your existing cards will still work, so there's no need to apply for a new one. The loan limit stays at twelve books, which most of you told us was plenty. And you've always been able to return books to any branch in the county, so nothing has changed there. The new service is that you can now renew your loans by text message. Just send the number on the back of your card, and you'll get a reply within a minute.

I know you'll also want to hear about overdue fines. When this was first discussed, the plan was to stop charging children and to keep the fines for adults. But the council looked at how much it cost to collect such small sums, and decided to go further. So from today, nobody pays a fine for a late book, whatever their age. We'd simply ask you to bring books back when you've finished with them.

Upstairs, there are six new study rooms. They aren't just for students, as some people have suggested. Anyone over sixteen may use them, and they're free of charge at any time of day. But they're small, and we expect them to be very popular, so you do have to reserve one online, at least a day in advance. Please don't just turn up and hope.

Finally, we're looking for volunteers. Our children's story sessions are well covered, thanks to a wonderful team of retired teachers, and the computer classes are taught by staff from the local college. Where we really need your help is our home delivery service. There are over two hundred people in this town who can't get to the library because of age or illness, and we need drivers to take books to them.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20.
Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20.

Now, let's look at the plan of the ground floor. I'd like you to imagine that you've just come in through the main entrance, which is in the middle of the south wall, at the bottom of your plan. Straight ahead of you, in the centre of the building, is the reception desk.

Let's start with what everyone asks about first, the café. It's the room immediately to your right as you come through the doors, so you can get a coffee without walking through the library at all. Beyond the café, in the south-east corner, is a meeting room that local groups can hire.

If you turn left at the entrance instead, you'll walk past the cloakroom. Keep going to the very end, and in the south-west corner you'll find the children's library. We put it there so that the noise won't travel to the reading areas.

Now go back to the reception desk. On the west side of the hall, to the left of reception as you face it, there's a large room full of armchairs. That's where you'll find the newspapers and magazines.
Directly across the hall from it, on the east side, is the computer area. There are thirty machines in there, and you can book them at reception.

And finally, the local history room. Go round the reception desk to the staircase, at the north end of the building. Many people expect to find local history to the left of the stairs, because that's where it used to be, but that room is now the staff office. The collection has moved to the other side, so you'll find it in the north-east corner.
That is the end of Part 2. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

What new service is available to library members?

options.A: borrowing more books at one time

items.stem: What must people do in order to use a study room?

options.B: book a room on the internet

options.A: take books to people at home.

groups.limit: Write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 16–20.

questions.explain:
答案是 A。Karen 說 surveyors inspected the building and found that the old roof was no longer safe，對應 the condition of the roof。
陷阱：B、C 都是 Many people assumed／others told me 的傳聞，緊接著 Neither is true 一次否定兩個選項。
questions.quote: Many people assumed we simply wanted room for more computers, and others told me they'd heard that visitor numbers had collapsed. Neither is true... The work became necessary when surveyors inspected the building and found that the old roof was no longer safe.
